conviction_note: No company-level unpriced number found: consensus ($3.35-3.37 EPS, $1.47-1.48bn sales) sits on the mechanics of the company's own unchanged guide, so the lean comes from positioning (+9.7% in 5 days off a 52-week low on light volume, downside-paid skew, beats sold on both 2026 prints) and from soft proxies that partly offset (record summer heat up, Pentair channel destock down). Hence p_up 45 on a full option-implied 6.5% move, giving -0.65; the findings sum to -1.2 because the positioning finding carries its own size and the panel should read the two numbers separately.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $3.37 and revenue $1.48bn (+1.5% y/y), EBIT $172.3m (Tiger preview 2026-10-16, https://www.itiger.com/news/1105406050); Earnings Whispers $3.35 / $1.47bn (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/POOL). Company guide: FY2026 adjusted EPS $10.87-11.17 unchanged on 2026-07-23 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000945841/000119312526313430/pool-ex99_1.htm). H1 adjusted EPS was 1.45 + 5.38 = 6.83, so the guide implies H2 EPS of $4.04-4.34 against H2 2025's 3.40 + 0.84 = 4.24. Rebuilding Q3 from the guide's own inputs (gross margin -30bp to about 29.3%, opex +3%, sales +1.5%) gives EBIT of about $173m, which matches consensus. The bar is sourced to two agreeing estimate sources and is consistent with the company guide.
positioning_check: Short interest 3,637,916 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up from 3,312,062 on 09-15, with days to cover 3.93 (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/pool/shortinterest). Against 36.34m shares outstanding (10-Q cover page, 2026-07-23) that is about 10% of shares: moderate, not the 18-23% crowded-short zone. Baseline: 25-delta skew +3.08 vol points (downside paid), put/call open-interest ratio 5.88, event-implied move 6.5% against a 3.0% median historical reaction. Spot $173.49 is 42.7% below the 52-week high and 12.6% above the low, up 9.72% over 5 days and 4.13% over 20 days. The 5-day rally came off a 52-week low of about $155.3 on 2026-10-07; MarketBeat reported a +7.4% day on 2026-10-15 on volume about 45% below average, attributed only to a Zacks expected-beat note (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-pool-nasdaq-pool-stock-jumps-74-time-to-buy-2026-10-15/).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is long-leaning after a news-less rally while the option market still pays for downside. The stock rose from a 52-week low of about $155.3 (2026-10-07) to $173.49, +9.7% in 5 sessions. The +7.4% day on 10-15 came on volume about 45% below average and was attributed only to a Zacks expected-beat note. Skew is +3.08 (downside paid) and the put/call OI ratio is 5.88. On both 2026 prints a beat was sold: Q1 EPS $1.45 vs about $1.35 went -2.37%, Q2 $5.38 vs about $5.33 went -6.55%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: the last 7 prints were -6.55, -2.37, -14.48, +0.91, +3.00, -6.66 and +1.01. The two 2026 beats (Q1, Q2) were sold, and the in-line or confirm-guide quarters of 2025 moved about +1 to +3.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up itself prices an expected beat that the consensus EPS ($3.37, -0.6% y/y) does not carry, so the stock now needs more than an in-line print. If the market had priced the risk of 'in-line, guide reconfirmed', the 5-day run-up would not sit at +9.7% on thin volume with no company news.
findings.independence: The baseline skew (+3.08) and P/C OI 5.88 come from a separate source (Yahoo option chain, in the sealed baseline). Counterweight: short interest of about 10% with 3.9 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/pool/shortinterest) is a squeeze mechanism on an in-line print, so the size has been shrunk for it.

findings.finding: Pentair, the largest pool-equipment supplier to POOL, cut channel inventory with 'major channel partners' by about $170m in Q2 (Pool segment sales -42%), guided Q3 Pool sales down 23-25%, and expects channel inventory to normalise by the end of Q3. BNP's analyst tied this to POOL, Pentair's largest customer. This implies POOL bought far less equipment in Q3, which can weigh on purchase-volume vendor incentives and gross margin. POOL's CFO said on 2026-07-23 that nothing Pentair reported changed the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin has been the line: Q2 2026's 30bp margin decline plus a lower GAAP guide went -6.55%, and Q4 2025's miss went -14.48%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EBIT of $172m equals the guide's mechanics, with gross margin at -30bp. If the market priced a destock-driven hit to vendor incentives or absorption, Q3 EPS consensus would sit below the guide-implied run-rate and not on it. Pentair's Q3 numbers (due 2026-10-27) are not yet out, so the size of the Q3 destock at POOL has not been confirmed.
findings.independence: Pentair Q3 guide of Pool -23-25% (Pentair Q2 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000042/q22026pressrelease.htm). Barclays' Fluidra downgrade cites POOL's 'record-high inventory' and US destocking (https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/fluidra-sa-MCE:FDR/news/barclays-cuts-fluidra-to-quot-equal-weight-quot-on-us-destocking-concerns-019e6dd4-a4f0-7d70-852c-93fc9b27145d/). Counterweight: lower inventory also means stronger Q3 operating cash flow, and the CFO explicitly excluded any Pentair effect from the guide (https://www.webull.com/news/15277450926826496). This is a proxy: no POOL document quantifies it.

findings.finding: Summer 2026 (June-August) was the hottest on record for the contiguous US per NOAA: +0.4F over the prior record, a record August, record-warm summers in AZ, NM, UT and CO, and record August heat in southern Florida. Hot weather lifts chemical and maintenance volumes, POOL's largest category, in Q3. POOL's CFO called July 'pretty much on point', and Q2 sales in CA, TX and AZ were down mid-single digits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on weather. The Q3 2025 print (sales +1%, EPS beat) went +0.91%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue growth of +1.5% is below the 2-3% H1 pace even before any weather effect, so a volume lift from record heat would show up as a revenue beat. The market has not credited it: the stock fell to a 52-week low on 10-07, a month after NOAA published.
findings.independence: NWS Tampa summer summary (https://www.weather.gov/media/tbw/climate/summaries/Aug_Summer2026_final.pdf) shows Florida sites in the top-ten warmest. Counterweight: Leslie's reported comps -6.2% to 2026-07-04 with weather and traffic cited (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821806/000119312526346961/lesl-ex99_1.htm), and chemical price deflation continues (Q2 chemicals -2%). This is a macro-to-company proxy that the company has not confirmed.

findings.finding: Leslie's, the largest pool-supply retailer and competitor to POOL's independent-dealer customers, filed prearranged Chapter 11 on 2026-09-30, closing 76 of 900+ stores, after comps of -6.2% in the quarter to 2026-07-04. That is market share freed for POOL's dealer and retail customers, and it is the first call on which management can comment on it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None: there is no prior competitor bankruptcy in the window.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock fell to its low a week after the filing, so the market treated it as a demand signal rather than a share-gain one. Any positive read needs management to say so on the call. The benefit falls mostly in Q4 and 2027.
findings.independence: Leslie's Q3 FY26 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821806/000119312526346961/lesl-ex99_1.htm), a different document from the same company. It cuts both ways: weak consumer pool demand (negative) and an ailing competitor (positive). Any POOL receivable exposure to Leslie's is unknown.

findings.finding: John Watwood, CEO since mid-2026, presents his second print and the last before his first full-year guide. The FY guide is $10.87-11.17 with consensus at about the midpoint. A new CEO narrowing to the low end, or resetting on a 2027 framing, is the guidance risk; Q2 already lowered the GAAP range by $0.21 of transition costs and the stock fell 6.55%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance prints dominate: Feb 2026 FY guide plus Q4 miss -14.48%, Jul 2026 GAAP guide cut -6.55%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits at the guide midpoint, about $11.0. If the market expected a narrowing to the low end, FY consensus would sit near $10.9.
findings.independence: Wells Fargo cut its target to $185 on 2026-09-11 and Deutsche Bank cut to $185 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-pool-nasdaq-pool-hits-new-52-week-low-whats-next-2026-10-07/). This is an inference, not a document: the 2026-10-09 8-K (St. Romain retirement effective 12-31) carries no business comment.

findings.finding: Buybacks slowed to $22.2m in Q2 (from $64.9m in Q1) with $580m of authorisation left, while the stock traded $155-190 through Q3. Any Q3 acceleration lowers the share count (36.34m on 2026-07-23) and supports EPS against a consensus that assumes little.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of -0.6% y/y implies little help from the share count. If Q3 buybacks were known to have accelerated, estimates would show EPS growth above net-income growth.
findings.independence: Q2 release: $580m remaining under the $600m authorisation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000945841/000119312526313430/pool-ex99_1.htm), the same company and a different document. Debt has already risen $110.8m to fund buybacks.

findings.finding: Q3 gross margin is guided down about 30bp y/y against a Q3 2025 comparison that expanded 50bp to 29.6%. H2 pricing slows to about 1% (FY about 2% after 3% in H1), chemical pricing deflation continues (Q2 chemicals -2%), and inbound freight recovery is not in the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 margin -30bp went -6.55% (with the GAAP guide cut); Q3 2025 margin +50bp went +0.91%.
findings.why_not_priced: This lands inside what the company guided, and consensus EBIT of $172.3m already embeds it. It matters only if margin comes in below -30bp, which nothing found here confirms.
findings.independence: Q2 release gross margin of 29.7% vs 30.0% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000945841/000119312526313430/pool-ex99_1.htm) and the Q3 2025 release at 29.6%, +50bp (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/945841/000119312525248060/pool-ex99_1.htm).

outside_window.finding: Pentair Q3 results on 2026-10-27 will quantify the end of the channel destock at its major distributor (POOL).

baseline_tension: What I found agrees with the downside-paid skew and cuts against the 5-day run-up: the rally has no company news under it and this name sold both of its 2026 beats. The moderate 10% short interest and a proxy-positive weather quarter are the counterweights, which is why p_up is 45 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): gross-margin finding -0.3 to -0.2, because it lands inside the company's own -30bp guide and consensus embeds it
Rule 5 (proxy smaller): record-heat weather finding +0.6 to +0.4, a macro-to-company proxy that the company and Leslie's comps do not confirm
Rule 3 (own caveat): CEO guidance-risk finding -0.4 to -0.3, because it is inference and the 8-K carries no business content
Rules 1 and 7 left the positioning finding at -1.0: it agrees with the skew and the beats-sold history, and moderate short interest (about 10%, 3.9 days) was already netted in
The sum is unchanged at -1.2 because the moves offset; abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged
